title: Intake classification and size-based routing
summary: Before a run starts, the supervisor MUST augment the request, estimate its implementation size, record a durable classification through `pan intake classify`, and start the route that record names unless the operator overrides it.
instructions: Before `pan init`, the supervisor MUST augment the preserved request under the prompt-augmentation skill and MUST write the result to `runtime/intake/<request-stem>/augmented.md`. The original request MUST stay verbatim and remains the reference for `intake.request_covered`.

The supervisor MUST estimate the request's implementation code under the sizing handbook: SLOC, TSSRFs, modules, the horizontal layers touched, and whether it adds a new integration point. It MUST NOT estimate test code, and it MUST round SLOC up when unsure.

The supervisor MUST record the estimate with `pan intake classify --request <request> --augmented <augmented> --rationale <text>` and its estimate options before `pan init`. The supervisor MUST NOT write or edit the classification record by hand.
The supervisor's first operator report MUST show the size class, layers touched, and integration and new-integration-point flags. It MUST also show the route and start the record names.

The supervisor MUST start the step the record names. A direct decomposition route starts `/pan-decompose` on the original request. The supervisor reads its recorded augmentation. Every other route starts `pan init` with the named workflow. `pan intake show --request <request>` prints the next command.

For a classified decomposition route, the supervisor MUST use the validated decomposition to start planning on the original request. The plan MUST produce an executable cohort plan with classified chunks. The supervisor MUST follow its cohort route after approval.

After the operator approves a successful classified prototype-trace, the supervisor MUST run `pan intake continue --run <trace-run-id>`. It MUST use the returned command and preserve the schema and trace output as references. A trace with no recorded continuation remains a standalone completed run.
When the operator names a workflow, that choice MUST win. The supervisor MUST record it with `--operator-workflow <workflow>` and MUST NOT reroute it.
When a route's workflow is not installed, classification refuses with `UNKNOWN_WORKFLOW`. The supervisor MUST report that refusal and MUST NOT invent a workflow.

A stage can report a breach of its class's SLOC hard max or a new unplanned integration point. Outside a one-shot implement stage, the supervisor MUST then reclassify with `pan intake classify --reason <text>`. The supervisor MUST report the new route. Rerouting an active run stays an operator-owned stage change.

A one-shot implement stage reports escalation when it exhausts the cycle bound, exceeds the S SLOC hard max, or cannot resolve a required decision. It can also pause at its implement try limit. In either case the supervisor MUST reclassify with `--reason` and MUST start the record's start. The supervisor MUST carry the latest one-shot implement output as evidence into that next run. A new integration point alone MUST NOT trigger that escalation.

Read this guidance before you augment an intake request.
